item.title: Observational constraints on a non-minimally coupled scalar field in non-metricity gravity with an extra degree of freedom
item.description: arXiv:2610.33146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a non-minimally coupled scalar field in non-metricity gravity, adopting a non-trivial connection class in spatially flat FLRW spacetimes. In contrast to the coincident-gauge choice, this connection class activates an additional dynamical degree of freedom (DoF) that modifies the background evolution. We study two representative models, defined by power-law and exponential coupling functions with the exponential potential for scalar field. Confronting both models with recent combined datasets - DESI BAO, two independent supernova compilations, and cosmic chronometers - we find that each reproduces an extended matter-dominated era followed by a stable late-time de-Sitter attractor, with inferred parameters consistent with the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. A complementary autonomous dynamical-system analysis identifies a sequence of critical points describing successive stiff-fluid, transient matter-dominated, and stable de-Sitter phases, ensuring a viable thermal history of the universe. The observational and dynamical results are mutually consistent and support the cosmological viability of the proposed models.
item.dc:creator: Saddam Hussain, Ghulam Murtaza, Avik De

item.title: A unified dark sector from a single canonical scalar field in Bohmian Wheeler-DeWitt cosmology with a cuscuton-inspired potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.33187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We quantize a spatially flat FLRW minisuperspace containing one canonical scalar field with the hyperbolic potential generated by a cuscuton-type superpotential, and extract cosmological histories from the Wheeler-DeWitt wave function in the de Broglie-Bohm interpretation. For the canonical potential parameter, related to the original cuscuton couplings, below an explicit critical value the potential has a unique nondegenerate minimum with positive height, and the ratio $\kappa$ of the scalar mass to the de Sitter Hubble rate at the minimum diverges as $\kappa^2\simeq 3b/\delta$, where $\delta$ is the relative distance to criticality. For the original hyperbolic potential, $\kappa\leq 3/\sqrt{2}$, whereas its cuscuton-inspired generalization allows a large hierarchy between scalar oscillation and expansion rates. For $\kappa\gg1$, small excitation and sufficiently large cell action, the reduced wave equation has an adiabatic Gaussian solution describing a de Sitter vacuum, a classical oscillating condensate whose averaged excitation density redshifts as $a^{-3}$, and, at the packet centre, a leading quantum density equal to the zero-point energy of the effective homogeneous oscillator divided by the physical cell volume, which is also dust-like. Full numerical solutions of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation support the averaged zero-point law at the reported $10^{-3}$ level, reproduce its dependence on the position of the Bohmian particle inside the packet, show that quantum corrections to the present Hubble rate converge as the inverse of the cell action, and support a single-field dust-plus-vacuum description at the homogeneous background level when $\kappa\gg1$. The classical histories approach the $\Lambda$CDM distance relations with a deviation of $1.3/\kappa$ in $D_V$. The dark energy component has $w=-1$ by construction, and the model is not fitted to data.
item.dc:creator: Anant Badal, Rikpratik Sengupta, Kaushik Bhattacharya

item.title: Black holes from a nonlocal equation of state: horizon geometry, singularity structure and thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.33222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a nonlocal equation of state for an anisotropic fluid reduces to a linear equation for the enclosed matter and uniquely selects a Yukawa-type density profile in a static, spherically symmetric Kerr--Schild geometry. The resulting neutral solution has finite-range hair, exponentially screened at large distances, with the asymptotic mass as its only conserved charge, and admits an exact horizon classification: horizonless configurations, Schwarzschild-like black holes, two-horizon geometries with a Cauchy horizon, and an extremal configuration whose mass and radius are obtained in closed form. We prove that the magnitude of the inner surface gravity exceeds that of the outer horizon throughout the two-horizon regime. When the central mass vanishes, the geometry approaches a global monopole in the static branch and a Kantowski--Sachs-type region in the nonstatic branch. The singularity satisfies Kr\'olak's strong-curvature criterion and is Tipler-strong along non-radial geodesics in the spacelike branch. For vanishing central mass, the Ricci scalar and the square root of the Kretschmann scalar are locally integrable with respect to the invariant spacetime volume, despite diverging at the origin. A power-law generalization of the nonlocal closure yields solutions expressed through incomplete gamma functions, interpolating between the singular core and a regular black hole with a de~Sitter core, without invoking nonlinear electrodynamics. We obtain closed-form surface gravities, an extended first-law identity and a Smarr relation, and locate the heat-capacity divergence using the lower branch of the Lambert function. Finally, thermodynamic topology distinguishes a Schwarzschild-like regime with one defect from an extremal regime with two opposite-winding defects that merge at the maximum Hawking temperature.
item.dc:creator: Hishan Farf\'an-Bachiloglu, C. R. Muniz, Francisco Tello-Ortiz

item.title: Hyperboloidal Initial Data with Prescribed Asymptotic Charges
item.description: arXiv:2610.33266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel method is introduced for constructing hyperboloidal initial data with direct analytic control over asymptotic charges prior to solving the Einstein constraint equations. Using the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the constraints together with a Fuchsian-analysis-inspired spectral solver, the asymptotic degrees of freedom, which determine infinite towers of asymptotic charges, including the Bondi energy and angular momentum, are used to prescribe the asymptotic behavior of solutions. As a proof of concept, we explicitly construct hyperboloidal initial data for a spinning black hole with Bondi energy $E_B = 2$ and angular momentum $J_B = 1/2$, starting from seed data induced on a hyperboloidal slice of the non-rotating Schwarzschild spacetime with mass $M=1$.
item.dc:creator: K\'aroly Csuk\'as, J\'anos \"Ost\"or, Istv\'an R\'acz

item.title: Impact of nonlinear electrodynamics on quasinormal modes of rotating black strings
item.description: arXiv:2610.33309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study massless scalar perturbations of rotating anti-de Sitter black strings sourced by a power-Maxwell field with negative exponent $s$. The charge enters the metric function as $-Qr^{p}$ with $p=2/(1-2s)$, and the case $s=-1/2$ gives a linear term with an algebraic horizon. Since rotation is a local boost of the static string, the rotating spectrum follows exactly from the static one evaluated at a frequency-dependent momentum. We compute the spectrum with the Horowitz-Hubeny series, Chebyshev collocation and time-domain evolution, each implemented in two independent codes and checked against the planar Schwarzschild-AdS limit. The charge acts in two ways. At the reduced charge $\hat q_c=0.72626$ the least damped pair of modes meets on the imaginary axis, so more strongly charged strings ring down without oscillation, and at the endpoint of the branch the spectrum is exactly hypergeometric. At large transverse momentum the distance of the modes from the light cone grows as $k^{1/(1-4s)}$, replacing the $k^{-1/5}$ law of the neutral brane. Rotation continues the exceptional point into a line in the plane of charge and rotation, adds a purely damped axisymmetric tower, and never produces superradiant growth. A near-horizon estimate used earlier for this geometry misses all of these effects.
item.dc:creator: F. S. Mirekhtiary, I. Sakalli

item.title: Neutron Star--Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.33314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The orbital evolution of a neutron star and a much lower-mass primordial black hole can differ strikingly from that of typical compact binaries. Dynamical tides, analogous to those in the Solar System's giant planet-moon systems, can accelerate inspiral or induce outspiral, depending on the orbital configuration. We show how gravitational-wave emission mediates this evolution when neutron star modes remain locked in resonance with the orbit. These effects may leave observable signatures in pulsar timing or gravitational waves.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Legred, Nicol\'as Yunes

item.title: Constraining Ultralight Dark Matter in Dynamical Dark Energy Cosmologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.33332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of scalar-field dark matter (SFDM) in a dynamical dark energy framework, extending previous analyses that considered SFDM within the standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmological model. We consistently implement the scenario at both the background and linear perturbation levels. We perform Bayesian parameter inference using Planck CMB measurements, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae to constrain the model parameter space. Our theoretical predictions show that lighter scalar-field masses produce increasingly strong scale-dependent suppression of matter fluctuations and more pronounced modifications to the CMB temperature power spectrum, whereas heavier masses progressively approach the cold dark matter limit. For the SFDM mass, we obtain a one-sided 95\% lower limit of $\log_{10}(m_\phi/{\rm eV})>-24.04$ from our main joint analysis. We find that replacing the standard cold dark matter fluid with SFDM does not qualitatively alter the constraints on dynamical dark energy or the evidence for its evolution, including a phantom crossing at low redshifts.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Awais, Hafiz Inam Ullah, Rafael C. Nunes, Paula S. Ferreira, Tonatiuh Matos

item.title: Accurate pulsar timing array likelihoods: better low-rank covariance for gravitational wave background
item.description: arXiv:2610.33444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In pulsar timing array analyses, the stochastic process describing the gravitational wave background is typically modeled using a Fourier basis at discrete frequencies with an interval $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, with a diagonal Fourier-domain covariance determined by the power spectral density at the corresponding frequencies. Although this rank-reduced modeling significantly accelerates likelihood evaluation and provides a good approximation in many scenarios, it can lead to biased parameter inference because it is insensitive to spectral features on scales smaller than $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. We introduce a better construction of the low-rank covariance for low-frequency processes by maximizing the log-likelihood averaged over an ensemble of realizations drawn from the true model likelihood. In this approach, the basis-domain covariance matrix is sensitive to the entire model spectrum and is generally non-diagonal. Using two mock datasets, we demonstrate improved likelihood accuracy and more faithful recovery of spectral features compared to the conventional Fourier-diagonal model. Benchmark tests show that this new model requires a computational cost comparable to that of the conventional approach.
item.dc:creator: Heling Deng, Ken D. Olum, Rutger van Haasteren

item.title: Acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.33481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and study its analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee theory by using Gross-Pitaevskii theory in the background of Schwarzschild-like spacetime. This black hole have two kinds of event horizons: one is the gravitational horizon $r_h=2M$(black hole horizon), the others are the internal and external acoustic horizons $2M<r_{ac-}\leq4M,\;r_{ac}\geq4M$(dumb hole horizon) which depend on the tuning parameter $\xi$ and Lorentz violation coupling constant $\ell$. The corresponding Hawking temperature $T_h$ depends only on $\ell$, however $T_{ac}$ depends on $\ell$ and $\xi$. The dumb hole temperature $T_{ac}$ has a maximum $T_{acm}=T_h/8$. When considering the scalar particles radiating from the dumb hole, we find that in low frequency, the grey-body factor increases with the tuning parameter $\xi$, but decreases with $\ell$. In the high frequency, it approaches to $1$. Its energy emission rate is similar to the Planck's black spectrum where there has a maximum at a given peak frequency $\omega_m$. The energy emission rate also increases with the tuning parameter $\xi$, but decreases with $\ell$. This opposite dependence relationship is the most experimentally valuable feature and can directly benchmark against observations of real astrophysical black holes.
item.dc:creator: Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Yu Shi, Yuehua Xiao, Jiliang Jing

item.title: Gravitational Waves from Ringing Dyonic Black Holes and Estimation of Parameters in Einstein-Bumblebee-Maxwell Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.33569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the quasinormal mode (QNM) frequencies of dyonic Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN)-like black holes associated with scalar and gravitational perturbations in the framework of Einstein-bumblebee-Maxwell gravity theory. The QNMs are calculated using the 6th-order Pad\'e averaged WKB approximation method. We analyse the dependence of oscillation frequencies and damping rate of the BHs for the free model parameters. To further verify the QNM spectrum, we study the time evolution of both the scalar and gravitational perturbations around the BHs and extract the dominant QNM from the resulting ringdown signal. Moreover, we try to estimate the BH parameters using Fisher analysis method for the future gravitational wave detector named Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We found that for supermassive BHs with mass around $10^6$ -- $10^8 M_\odot$ and at lower redshifts, the signal-to-noise ratio for the detection of a QNM signal by the LISA is high. Further, for a representative source at a luminosity distance of $3$ Gpc, the BH mass at the detector reference frame and the Lorentz violating parameter are well constrained for supermassive BHs with mass $\ge 10^6.$
item.dc:creator: Sikha Gogoi, Umananda Dev Goswami

item.title: A no-go theorem for closed timelike curves in globally null-foliated spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The study of closed timelike curves has proceeded one spacetime at a time, and the criteria available form three families, the time function criteria, the energy condition criteria, and the topological criteria. We initiate a fourth family of criteria, elementary in form and resting on a single scalar equation rather than any energy condition. We prove that a spacetime admitting a globally defined function whose gradient is everywhere null cannot contain a closed timelike curve, and that the hypothesis is logically independent of stable causality rather than weaker than it. The proof turns on one algebraic fact, that a null covector is never orthogonal to a timelike vector, so the function grows strictly along every timelike curve and cannot close. Because the null eikonal equation alone decides the criterion, we can use it where the classical time function theorem is silent. We establish for the first time that no Kundt spacetime and no Robinson--Trautman spacetime can contain a closed timelike curve on any region where the null coordinate is globally single valued, whatever the cosmological constant and the rotation one form, which settles a question left open for gyratonic waves. We further show that the Misner, Ori and Ahmed constructions reduce to the statement that a compact null direction has turned timelike, and that the cosmological constant, the expansion and the shear are spectators in all of them.
item.dc:creator: Hongsheng Zhang

item.title: Forecasting Strongly Lensed Binary Black Hole Rates from the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background with TianQin
item.description: arXiv:2610.33751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The millihertz stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) provides a population-level probe of stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs) and their cosmic merger history. We develop a framework using TianQin alone to propagate SGWB-informed BBH population constraints into forecasts of strongly lensed BBH mergers detectable by ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. The framework distinguishes between lensed events with at least one detected image and lens systems in which both images are detected and successfully associated. Using a one-year mock observation, we infer the BBH population and propagate the resulting posterior through a galaxy-scale lensing model with image-level selection. For the adopted system-magnification threshold, \(\mu_{\rm sys}\ge 2\), the median predicted rate of lensed events with at least one detected image is \(R_{\rm event}^{\rm det}=5.50\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}\), while the median rate of associated two-image lens systems is \(R_{\rm sys}^{\rm det}=2.54\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}\); the median detectable system fraction is \(\mathcal{F}_{\rm sys}^{\rm det}=3.35\times10^{-4}\). Compared with the prior-only propagation, the pooled 16th--84th percentile widths decrease by 6.5\% for the event rate, 6.4\% for the system rate, and 4.0\% for the system fraction. Our work establishes a quantitative link between millihertz SGWB inference and forecasts of strongly lensed BBH mergers for ground-based gravitational-wave observations.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Cheng Liang

item.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.33883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Pad\'e approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta

item.title: Gravitational Radiation Coupled to a real massive scalar Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.33928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of small-data global solutions to the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system with a positive-mass real scalar field in wave gauge. We show that the linearized trace component of the metric perturbation admits a $\hat t^{-1}\simeq t^{-1}$ optimal decreasing rate. Moreover, a quantitative one-point observability estimate is established: the initial Klein-Gordon energy is controlled by this leading order coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Yue Ma, Xianghao Wu, Weidong Zhang

item.title: Comment on "Effect of perfect fluid dark matter..." [Phys. Dark Univ. 34 (2021) 100891]
item.description: arXiv:2610.34019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This Comment clarifies the physical interpretation of the black hole spacetime metric employed by Shaymatov \textit{et al.} [Phys. Dark Univ. 34 (2021) 100891]. We point out that the metric, originally derived in Li and Yang (2012), describes a specific dual-component system consisting of cold dark matter and a phantom field background. Treating this geometry as a single-component ``Perfect Fluid Dark Matter'' (PFDM) with a total equation of state $w_{\mathrm{total}} = -1$ is physically incompatible with the gravitational attraction required for dark matter halos. Furthermore, we clarify the distinct parameter regimes of the original model to prevent potential misapplications in extreme astrophysical scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Hsun Li, Kwei-Chou Yang

item.title: Repetitive Magnetic Penrose Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.34164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonlinear iterative repetitive Penrose process established recently by Ruffini et al.\ is generalized to the magnetic Penrose process. The spacetime background is the Kerr metric, the external magnetic field is described by the Wald solution, the electromagnetic field is treated as a test field, and the charge is treated as a test charge. We analyze the optimal conditions for maximum energy extraction on the equatorial plane and find that under these conditions the core mechanism of the iterative process is charging feedback. After charging, the black hole charge is approximately half of the Wald charge. When the neutral parent particle decays, charge conservation forces the infalling fragment to carry charge while the other fragment carries the opposite charge, so the black hole charge accumulates monotonically. The monopole voltage of the Wald solution decreases linearly with the charge $Q$ and crosses zero to reverse sign at a certain point, so the magnetic gain is gradually neutralized by the charge. The repetitive magnetic Penrose process is therefore forced to terminate and eventually falls back to the mechanical Penrose process. The energy extraction efficiency $>100\%$ predicted by the single magnetic Penrose process will therefore be prevented.
item.dc:creator: Ke Wang, Xin-Yun Hu, Xiao-Xiong Zeng

item.title: Finite-Distance Imaging of Relativistic Equilibrium Tori around Genuine Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.34331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate finite-distance images of stationary, pressure-supported tori around genuine, electrically neutral Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson black holes using general relativistic ray tracing with gray emission and absorption. The emitting volume is bounded by a constant-specific-angular-momentum equilibrium free surface, and the observer is placed at a radius of $50M$. Along the investigated external-field sequence, integrated brightness and apparent size both increase strongly as the field modifies the equilibrium source and photon propagation. Higher torus filling has a different effect: in a representative sequence, brightness grows by a factor of $5.9$ while the intensity-weighted image size increases by only $10\%$. Increasing viewing inclination enhances lateral brightness contrast. Stronger self-absorption can coexist with higher absolute brightness because emission and absorption scale together in the adopted gray prescription. At common pressure center and filling, increasing the dimensionless spin from $0.5$ to $0.95$ dims the retrograde sequence by a factor of about $7$ as its equilibrium contracts, whereas prograde brightness changes by only $2\%$. These contrasting responses show how the equilibrium boundary, fluid motion, and optical depth jointly shape the brightness, scale, and asymmetry of finite-distance torus images.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Peng Yan, Xiang-Qian Li, Xiao-Jun Yue

item.title: Topological analysis of novel charged-AdS black hole solutions embedded in dark matter halos with quintessence field
item.description: arXiv:2610.34334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the properties of a charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole in the presence of a NGC 4649-type dark matter halo and a surrounding quintessence field. Starting from the modified Einstein field equations (EFEs), we construct the corresponding black hole solutions by incorporating the effects of electric charge, cosmological constant, dark matter distribution, and quintessence characterized by a variable equation of state. We analyze the resulting spacetime geometry through the metric function and horizon structure, showing that the dark matter halo strengthens the gravitational attraction, whereas the quintessence field provides a repulsive contribution that substantially alters the asymptotic behavior of the spacetime. Furthermore, the thermodynamic properties are investigated by applying the Duan-\(\phi\)-mapping topological theory together with the generalized free energy method. This framework allows us to examine the topological structure, critical behavior, and stability conditions of the black hole system in a consistent manner. We further study the fractional shifts relative to the reference value of \(\omega_q\) and observe that variations in \(\omega_q\) produce systematic changes which highlight the important role of the quintessence field in determining the phase structure and critical behavior of the black hole system.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Yasir, Hafiza Bushra Mujahid, Faisal Javed, Shahid Qaisar

item.title: Geometric criticality and regular quasibound spectra of axial Proca fields in Schwarzschild spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.34528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how a local geometric critical point of the odd-parity Proca potential relates to the global quasibound spectrum in Schwarzschild spacetime. After normalization by $\mu^2$, the axial potential $V_{\rm ax}=(1-2M/r)[\ell(\ell+1)/r^2+\mu^2]$ has the same radial form as the timelike-geodesic effective potential. Its outer minimum and inner maximum merge at $r=6M$, the Schwarzschild innermost stable circular orbit, when $(M\mu_c)^2=\ell(\ell+1)/12$. With $\delta=1-(M\mu)^2/(M\mu_c)^2$, we derive exact fold scalings: stationary-point separation $\propto\delta^{1/2}$, barrier--well depth $\propto\delta^{3/2}$, and curvature magnitudes $\propto\delta^{1/2}$. Continued-fraction calculations for the first three axial quasibound branches with $\ell=1,2,3$, cross-checked for selected modes by independent Riccati shooting, show regular frequency continuation across the threshold and approximately linear near-critical behavior. At fixed radius the radial operator is affine in $\delta$, supporting a conditional simple-root analytic interpretation. The main result is the explicit distinction between geometric potential criticality and spectral degeneracy for the branches examined.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Sousa Ribeiro, Francisco Artur Pinheiro Alves Junior

item.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted H\"older estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy

item.title: Exact spinning wormholes in five dimensions from Toda integrability
item.description: arXiv:2610.34672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a new exact solution to the five-dimensional Einstein-phantom-scalar system that describes a rotating wormhole connecting two asymptotically flat regions. The solution represents a rotating generalization of the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole with equal angular momenta. Under the cohomogeneity-one ansatz, we demonstrate that the radial equations reduce to an integrable $A_1\oplus A_2$ Toda system, from which the general local solution can be obtained in closed form. This integrable structure enables us to implement the regularity and asymptotic-flatness conditions analytically, thereby singling out a three-parameter family of solutions characterized by the mass, the equal angular momenta, and the scalar charge. The resulting spacetimes are geodesically complete, horizonless and stably causal, and contain no curvature singularities. The Toda structure further allows us to prove the uniqueness of the wormhole throat and to derive a sharp upper bound on the angular momentum for a fixed throat area. We also establish the existence and uniqueness of an ergosurface with respect to the stationary frame that is nonrotating at one asymptotic end, while the opposite end rotates relative to this frame. In a suitable scaling limit, the scalar field vanishes and the solution approaches the exterior region of the extremal Myers-Perry black hole with equal angular momenta.
item.dc:creator: Masato Nozawa

item.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.
item.dc:creator: Bobby Eka Gunara

item.title: Quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R,T)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.35096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study tensor perturbations and quasinormal modes (QNMs) of thick branes in $f(R,T)=R+\alpha T$ gravity. Starting from the background thick brane solutions, we derive the Schr\"odinger-like equation for gravitational perturbations and construct the corresponding effective potential. The effective potential exhibits a double-barrier structure whose properties depend on the model parameters. We analyze transmission spectra and find good agreement between resonance peaks and the real parts of the quasinormal frequencies. The parameters $b$ and $\alpha$ mainly control the width and height of the potential barriers, respectively. QNMs are extracted using both time-domain evolution and direct integration methods, showing consistent results for low-lying modes. Higher overtones become increasingly difficult to extract due to stronger damping and numerical contamination. Our results indicate that $f(R,T)$ corrections significantly affect both the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum, providing a possible imprint of modified gravity in braneworld perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Peng E, Hai-Long Jia, Chun-Chun Zhu

item.title: An asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.35248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we construct an asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity. Starting from a linear choice of the reduced function, which yields an asymptotically conical Schwarzschild-like solution, we introduce a nonlinear deformation that preserves the leading asymptotic cone while producing an exact black hole solution with a de Sitter core and finite curvature invariants. We further establish the corresponding black hole thermodynamics for both solutions within the Hamiltonian and Wald frameworks. The entropy contains rational and logarithmic terms in the regular model, and both solutions satisfy the first law of black hole thermodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Zhou Liu, Shao-Wen Wei, Yu-Xiao Liu

item.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
item.description: arXiv:2610.35253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matsui

item.title: From Specific Heat Bounds to Penrose-like Inequalities: A Unified Thermodynamic Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2610.35264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under explicit and physically motivated assumptions, we identify a local-to-global thermodynamic mechanism that organizes several previously disconnected inequalities on black holes. We first focus on asymptotically flat, static, and spherically-symmetric black holes, and provide a unified thermodynamic perspective on various Penrose-like inequalities. We also discuss the generalizations in asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes/branes. In holographic settings, these bounds imply monotonic behavior of normalized thermodynamic quantities in the dual field theory. Notably, one central integrated inequality can be established directly under the NEC in general static planar symmetric asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black branes. Our purpose is not to claim a fully general proof of the proposed local bounds, but to expose a unified structural perspective connecting local thermodynamic constraints to global geometric inequalities. Establishing the local bounds beyond the classes considered here remains an open problem.
item.dc:creator: Kai-Peng Lu, H. Lu, Run-Qiu Yang

item.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures and Periodic Orbits of Charged Particles Around a Five-Dimensional Rotating Black Hole: Comparison with the Kerr Black Hole
item.description: arXiv:2610.35386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study periodic orbits of charged particles in the equatorial plane of a five-dimensional ($D=5$) rotating Myers--Perry black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field, and the gravitational waves emitted by these orbits in an extreme mass-ratio inspiral. All results are compared with the Kerr BH in the uniform magnetic field. We find that a charged particle is much more weakly bound to the $D=5$ dimensional BH, i.e. its energy at the innermost stable circular orbit is close to unity, $0.95$--$0.99$, compared with $0.78$--$0.94$ for the Kerr BH, and the depth of the potential well is several times smaller. As a result, the periodic orbits of the $D=5$ dimensional BH lie much closer to the separatrix. The magnetic field can make the azimuthal frequency of the orbit smaller than the radial one and produces loops in the orbits far from the BH. Using the numerical kludge method, we compute the gravitational waveforms for a compact object of $10M_\odot$ orbiting a BH of $10^6M_\odot$. At the same magnetic field, the $D=5$ dimensional signal has a longer period, lower frequencies, and an amplitude smaller by about $18\%$. We show that for the magnetic parameter $\beta M=0.02$ the strongest spectral line is at $7.9$\,mHz, compared with $9.9$\,mHz for the Kerr BH. An estimate of the radiation reaction shows that the periodic orbits survive from less than an hour to a few days in the presence of an external magnetic field. Over these lifetimes, the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA is $7$--$31$ for the rotating BH in $D=5$ dimensions, compared to the Kerr BH where it is about $15$--$54$.
item.dc:creator: Bahromjon Shokirov, Tursunali Xamidov, Chen Zhou, Sanjar Shaymatov, Chengxun Yuan

item.title: Phase-Space Constraints on a General Class of Eckart-like Viscous Cosmologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.35405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cosmological dynamics of a general class of viscous dark matter models using a dynamical system analysis. In the Eckart formalism, these viscous cosmologies are characterized by a dimensionless bulk viscous pressure $\Omega_\Pi \equiv \Omega_\Pi(\Omega_m)$, where $\Omega_m$ is the matter density parameter. Our analysis demonstrates that a viable early radiation era requires the complete absence of viscosity, a proper matter-dominated epoch demands a small viscous pressure, and the only physically admissible late-time attractor is the cosmological constant-dominated fixed point; consequently, the background expansion must closely track standard $\Lambda$CDM evolution. We validate these general results using the power-law parameterization $\Omega_\Pi = -\hat{\xi}_0 \Omega_m^s$, where $\hat{\xi}_0$ and $s$ are real parameters; for $s \geq 1$ and $\hat{\xi}_0 \ll 1$, the model reproduces the $\Lambda$CDM background, while for $s < 1$ the system encounters a past-time integration boundary where the dark matter density transitions into negative values and its viscous pressure evaluates to nonphysical complex numbers. Since the background expansion essentially duplicates $\Lambda$CDM, the model is unlikely to resolve the $H_0$ tension. However, large differences arise at the linear perturbative level; indeed, on sub-horizon scales, bulk viscosity causes a scale-dependent dissipative drag on the matter density fluctuations; this increases the Hubble friction, offering a channel to suppress structure growth.
item.dc:creator: David R. Moreno (Universidad Industrial de Santander), J. Bayron Orjuela-Quintana (Universidad del Valle), Yeinzon Rodriguez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Universidad Antonio Narino)

item.title: Decoupled asymmetric thin-shell wormholes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct reflection-asymmetric thin-shell wormholes by joining a Schwarzschild exterior to its minimal geometric deformation, which shares the same mass and redshift function, so that the asymmetry is carried entirely by the gravitational-decoupling sector. The deformed side is a black hole sourced by a scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, in its branch with a real scalar. We show that the total radial null energy of shell and bulk obeys an exact identity and becomes positive for a sufficiently strong deformation. The momentum flux across the shell equals the radial null-energy density of the bulk, and retaining it yields the linear stability condition in closed form. We prove that stability with a conventional shell response requires the bulk to violate the radial null energy condition at the throat; the deformation instead enlarges the stable domain and moves the transition radius inside the photon sphere. For a stationary extension built on Kerr, the junction is solved exactly in the spin, which fixes how the angular momentum is shared between shell and bulk and where the shell behaves as a rotating fluid. A free-precession model provides an estimate of the gravitational-wave signal of the throat.
item.dc:creator: A. L\'opez-Hormaz\'abal, Hishan Farf\'an-Bachiloglu, Kazuharu Bamba, Francisco Tello-Ortiz

item.title: Quasibound modes of rotating acoustic black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a metric describing rotating acoustic black holes in spherical coordinates. This formulation allows us to obtain exact analytical solutions of the massless Klein--Gordon equation governing scalar perturbations in the corresponding background spacetime. By imposing the appropriate boundary conditions, we derive an exact analytical expression for the quasibound state frequencies of the system. Quasibound states play a central role in the dynamics of black hole analog systems, as they characterize long-lived resonant modes trapped in the vicinity of the effective horizon. Their investigation provides valuable insights into wave propagation, mode stability, and energy confinement in analog spacetimes. Moreover, because acoustic black holes offer experimentally accessible realizations of horizon physics, the study of quasibound states may establish a direct connection between theoretical predictions and laboratory observations, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of phenomena that also arise in gravitational black hole environments.
item.dc:creator: H. S. Vieira, V. B. Bezerra

item.title: Gravitationally Induced Polarization-Angle Rotation in Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.35589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio pulsars emit highly polarized radiation whose polarization properties are commonly described by the Rotating Vector Model (RVM). In this work, we investigate the effects of gravitational light bending and parallel transport on the polarization profile of a pulsar in a hypothetical binary system with a black hole (BH) companion. We combine the RVM with numerical integration of null geodesics to calculate the polarization direction along the photon trajectory and model the orbital-phase-dependent variation of the observed polarization position angle (PPA). We consider both non-spinning and spinning black hole companions and include the evolution of the orbital geometry due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. For a non-spinning black hole, the change in the observed polarization direction arises from the geometric shift associated with gravitational light bending. For a spinning black hole, frame dragging introduces an additional geometric shift, while parallel transport produces an additional polarization rotation measured relative to our chosen reference construction. We investigate the dependence of these polarization changes on the binary parameters and the orientation of the pulsar spin. We find that gravitational light bending can significantly distort the characteristic S-shaped PPA profile, particularly near superior conjunction, and can reverse its overall sense of variation for the supermassive black hole system considered here. Relativistic spin-orbit evolution also affects the orbital-phase dependence of the polarization profile, particularly in the supermassive black hole system. These results show that relativistic photon propagation can modify both the shape and the phase dependence of pulsar polarization profiles and may provide a useful probe of the geometry of pulsar-BH binaries when such systems are discovered.
item.dc:creator: Jyotijwal Debnath, Amodio Carleo, Delphine Perrodin, Pratik Tarafdar

item.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.35602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.
item.dc:creator: Guangzhou Guo, Zhen Pan

item.title: Lunar tidal response-induced clock frequency variations on the Moon
item.description: arXiv:2610.33117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As clock performance improves, the instability and uncertainty of the clock's fractional frequency shift (FFS) become comparable to the FFS caused by the lunar tidal response (LTR), so the influence of the LTR on lunar time needs to be investigated. In this paper, we used the Keplerian expansions method to study the FFS to the level of $10^{-18}$ caused by the LTR between two clocks placed in different positions on the Moon. We consider the case of the Moon orbiting in an elliptical orbit, which is closer to the actual situation compared to the case of the Moon moving in a circular orbit. An interesting phenomenon is found that the longitude difference between two clocks can cause a change in the amplitude and phase of the FFS due to the LTR, but the latitude difference only changes the amplitude of the FFS. We further estimated the clock difference between two clocks near the Moon caused by the LTR. When one clock is on the lunar surface, and the other is on the Earth's surface, the LTR will cause a clock difference of $% -5.68\times 10^{-7}$ $\mu $s/day between the two clocks. These are significant for the construction of a lunar time and clock synchronization near the Moon.
item.dc:creator: Hongbin Zhang, Baocheng Zhang

item.title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2610.33141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Lawrie, Simon Horsley

item.title: Dark Matter phase space distribution under a fully relativistic treatment. Eddington inversion according to general relativity
item.description: arXiv:2610.33150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a fully relativistic extension of Eddington inversion to reconstruct the phase-space distribution function of dark matter from its density profile. Treating dark matter as an effective perfect fluid in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, we use the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to determine the gravitational background and derive an Abel-type inversion that yields the distribution function in terms of the conserved particle energy measured at infinity. We show that the resulting expression recovers the classical Eddington inversion in the weak-field, nonrelativistic limit. We also investigate the finite-boundary contribution, which can introduce an unphysical divergence, and present a regularization procedure that removes it. We apply our method to a Milky Way model consisting of a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White halo and a Gondolo-Silk dark-matter spike around Sagittarius A$^*$, neglecting baryonic contributions. The relativistic and Newtonian velocity distributions agree at radii far from the Galactic center but begin to differ at distances of order $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{pc}$. Closer to the black hole, the relativistic peak speed can reach approximately twice the Newtonian prediction. Finally, we derive a general expression for dark-matter capture by neutron stars that accommodates arbitrary ambient velocity distributions. Near Sagittarius A$^*$, the relativistic capture factor is nearly an order of magnitude smaller than the Maxwell-Boltzmann prediction, while the Newtonian Eddington result can overestimate it by a factor of approximately two. These results demonstrate the importance of relativistic phase-space reconstruction for dark-matter phenomenology in strong gravitational fields.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Hoefken Zink, Pellegrino Piantadosi

item.title: The Hosts and Mass Distribution Function of the Most Massive Black Holes: Implications for the nHz Gravitational Wave Background
item.description: arXiv:2610.33162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the core-radius, $r_\gamma,$ of a galaxy's central core along with a volume-limited sample of brightest cluster galaxies (BCG) to determine the $z=0$ mass distribution function of the most massive super-massive black holes (SMBH). We recover a $M_{BH}-r_\gamma$ relationship between the SMBH mass, $M_{BH},$ and $r_\gamma$ of form $M_{BH} \approx1.3\times10^{10}~(r_\gamma/{\mathrm{kpc}})~M_\odot,$ with $\sigma = 0.25\pm0.03$ dex scatter in $M_{BH}.$ We derive a core distribution function (CDF), based on HST and DLS images of the BCGs. The CDF falls steeply as $N(r_\gamma)\sim r_\gamma^{-3}$ for $r_\gamma>0.50$ kpc. Only $\sim5\%$ of BCGs have $r_\gamma>1$ kpc. Combining the CDF and $M_{BH} - r_\gamma$ relationship yields the BH mass distribution function (MDF). For $M_{BH} \geq 7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ (the mean $M_{BH}$ at $r_\gamma=0.50$ kpc) we derive: $\log\left(\frac{dN(M_{BH})}{d{M_{BH}/10^{10} M_\odot}}~[\rm Mpc^{-3}]\right)=(-3.05\pm0.42)~\log\left(\frac{M_{BH}}{10^{10}M_\odot}\right)~-~5.11\ (+0.41, -0.36)$. Cores with $r_\gamma \geq 0.50$ kpc are found almost exclusively in BCGs, implying that SMBHs with $M_{BH} \geq7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ may also be exclusive to BCGs. Core-radius correlates with $\alpha,$ a parameter that characterizes the growth of BCG envelopes by mergers, suggesting that the most massive SMBHs grew in tandem with their BCG hosts. The BH MDF embodies a significant population of SMBH with $M_{BH} >7\times10^{9} M_\odot.$ When combined with the Liepold & Ma (2024) BH MDF to account for SMBH with $M_{BH} < 7\times10^{9} M_\odot,$ it can comfortably explain the nHz gravitational wave background.
item.dc:creator: Marc Postman, Tod R. Lauer, Daniel J. D'Orazio, Bellamy Bailey

item.title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.33220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Pablo L. Saldanha, Nelson Yokomizo

item.title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusci\'el and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.
item.dc:creator: Aren Martinian

item.title: Catastrophe Structure and Stability of Axion Stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.33549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Axion stars are self-gravitating Bose--Einstein condensates of QCD axions or axion-like particles. Their stability determines whether they can survive as dark-matter structures and what astrophysical signatures they may produce. Here we combine a non-relativistic Schr\"odinger--Poisson description with catastrophe theory to develop a unified picture of axion-star stability. Beginning with the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system for a periodic axion potential, we derive the effective equations of motion and conserved quantities and construct a one-parameter family of star-like solutions. A Gaussian variational ansatz reduces the problem to an analytic energy functional $E(R;N)$. Within this model, equilibria appear and disappear through Arnold $A_2$, $A_3$, and $A_4$ catastrophes as the particle number $N$ and interaction strengths vary. A repulsive sextic interaction produces two stable branches---dilute and dense axion stars---separated by an unstable branch. The same catastrophe criteria apply beyond the sextic truncation: for the full cosine and QCD-corrected potentials, the fold conditions follow from the complete variational energy and can be evaluated numerically. We also separate stability within the collective-coordinate ansatz from full radial perturbative stability and specify the range in which the non-relativistic treatment is reliable. This framework provides a compact classification of axion-star phases and identifies model-dependent critical masses associated with collapse, bosenova-like emission, and black-hole formation.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Kusmartsev, Fedor V., Joudy JF Beek, and Jack CM Hughes. "Catastrophe structure and stability of axion stars." Physical Review D 114, no. 8 (2026): 083032
item.dc:creator: Fedor V Kusmartsev, Joudy J F Beek, Jack C M Hughes

item.title: Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[ (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $\phi(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[ \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}\phi=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $\phi(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.
item.dc:creator: Pieter-Bart Peters

item.title: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands
item.description: arXiv:2610.33865v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-energy outbursts from magnetars may be associated with crustal failures or quakes. The magnetoelastic modes of the star can be excited to large amplitudes in such a framework, providing a natural explanation for the quasi-periodic oscillations observed in the X-ray tails of some events. However, previous calculations of torsional modes have been carried out assuming an intact crust without accounting for the failure itself. We develop a code in this paper that solves the axial sector of the linearised Einstein-Maxwell-Euler equations in a cavity that hosts inelastic regions or 'plastic islands'. As crustal elements are displaced, shear stresses are tracked as a function of time to allow cells to dynamically switch from elastic to inelastic states. The presence of islands in the crust promotes phase mixing and, when reflected waves mix constructively, large sections fail collectively ('avalanche') if the initial kick is strong enough. Transient spectral features are observed as a result of the progressive loss of elastic support, which may explain the temperamental nature of the oscillations observed following giant flares and magnetar storms.
item.dc:creator: Arthur G. Suvorov

item.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.34024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $\kappa$. At large $|\kappa|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|\kappa|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $\kappa$ drops below a critical value.
item.dc:creator: Maxim Zelenko, Dam Thanh Son

item.title: Exact lattice bosonization of the double-scaled $c=1$ matrix model
item.description: arXiv:2610.34376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a recent paper by two of us, it has been shown that entanglement entropy (EE) of matrix quantum mechanics (or, equivalently, of a non-relativistic fermion model) has a natural interpretation in terms of an exact bosonization of the fermion theory in terms of a lattice boson with lattice spacing $\sim 1/N$ (where $N$ is the rank of the matrix, equal to the number of fermions). The theory of this lattice boson is distinct from a latticized version of the "collective variable'' theory which is formulated in terms of the fermion density $\rho(\lambda)$ ("collective variable''); it is, in fact, more closely related to the Wigner distribution of the fermions. In this paper, we develop this connection further for the $c=1$ double scaled matrix model. Even though $N$ becomes infinite, the double scaled theory is described by a boson on a finite and non-uniform lattice spacing, of order $\sim g_s(x) l_s$ (where $g_s(x) \equiv g_s {\rm cosech}^2(x/l_s)$ is a position dependent string coupling). We explicitly derive the $c=1$ EE, as well as the one and two-point functions of fermion density from the lattice boson. The results are explicitly finite, unlike the collective variable theory which is shown to yield divergent answers. Our results suggest that while local observables such as the EE and $\langle \rho(\lambda) \rangle$, are characterized by a unique short distance scale $g_s(x) l_s$, the asymptotic observables such as the S-matrix at every genus are characterized by a short distance scale $l_s$. We show how this arises and discuss a possible interpretation in terms of D0 brane physics.
item.dc:creator: Adwait Gaikwad, Gautam Mandal, Ajay Mohan

item.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
item.description: arXiv:2610.35117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically-unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids may rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole may therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.
item.dc:creator: Arthur G. Suvorov, Armen Sedrakian

item.title: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states
item.description: arXiv:2610.35183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit.
item.dc:creator: Yasusada Nambu

item.title: Theory and Cosmology of Biverse Volume-Normalized Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.35384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This dissertation expounds the biverse volume-normalized gravity, a novel theoretical framework of classical and quantum gravity that provides an unusual solution to the cosmological constant problem, the 60-degree-of-magnitude discrepancy between the value of the vacuum energy density in our universe predicted by particle physics and that implied by cosmological data. In the literature, there exist two interesting ideas: 1) to use the "volume-normalized" action functional, the usual action of the particle Standard Model and general relativity but divided by the spacetime volume, first proposed by Tseytlin; 2) to generate the vacuum energy density dynamically by assigning a ghost-free massive potential to the graviton. However, each has a problem: Tseytlin's attempt suffers from diverging quantum loops and the massive gravity theory has a second metric tensor with questionable origin and the quantum strong coupling problem. Inspired by these two ideas, as well as the AdS/CFT correspondence in string theory, the biverse volume-normalized gravity extends Tseytlin's idea by placing our (3+1)-dimensional universe on the boundary of a (4+1)-dimensional bulk space. This new adaptation controls the large quantum gravity loops in the limit of vanishing ratio of the spacetime volume of our universe to that of the other universe. The ghost-free massive gravity can then be seamlessly incorporated, not only that its otherwise nebulous second metric tensor appears naturally as the pullback of the bulk metric on the boundary, but its strong coupling problem also solved. The biverse volume-normalized gravity is also consistent with all tested models of particle cosmology and the evolution of the universe, and nontrivially predicts that the tensor-to-scalar ratio of our universe is exactly zero.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: Tidal contributions to neutron star orbital precession around Sgr $A^*$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate tidal contributions to the orbital precession of neutron stars around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, using stellar configurations described by the Tolman - Oppenheimer - Volkoff equations. We examine the dependence of tidal precession on stellar compactness, pericentre distance, and the quadrupolar tidal Love number $k_2$, and compare its magnitude with general relativistic orbital precession. The calculated tidal angular shift decreases strongly with increasing pericentre distance and, for the stellar configurations considered, with increasing compactness. Larger Love numbers enhance the tidal contribution. This behaviour reflects the strong dependence of tidal precession on the stellar-radius-to-pericentre-distance ratio, $(R/r_p)^5$. Despite the enhancement during closer encounters, the predicted tidal shifts remain extremely small, reaching approximately $3.5 \times 10^{-18},\mu as$ within the displayed parameter range. The ratio of tidal to general relativistic precession spans approximately $10^{-33}$ - $10^{-28}$, indicating that relativistic precession overwhelmingly dominates. Our results suggest that direct detection of the neutron-star tidal contribution through orbital precession around Sgr A* would be exceptionally challenging under the assumptions of the adopted model.
item.dc:creator: H Lalrinfela, P. C. Lalremruati, Zodinmawia, N Malsawmtluangi

item.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.35836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

item.title: Naive Quantum Gravity
item.description: arXiv:1502.02058v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A possible alternative route to a quantum theory of gravity is described. The usual path quantises the gravitational field in order to introduce the statistical structure characteristic of quantum mechanics. The procedure followed here instead is to remove the probabilistic element of quantum theory by using the less-common technique of introducing final boundary conditions as well as initial on the source. The relevant quantum formalism then becomes compatible with the non-statistical nature of general relativity and a viable theory can be constructed without difficulty. The view taken here is that the lack of both experimental guidance and theoretical consensus lends justification to considering such less mainstream ideas.

item.title: Lorentz violation and Hawking--Page metastability in Bumblebee--AdS gravity
item.description: arXiv:2411.06188v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The standard Hawking--Page description of AdS black holes, based on an on-shell Gibbs free-energy crossing, does not resolve the metastable black-hole branch or the barrier-mediated conversion between competing phases. We address this issue for neutral AdS black holes in Bumblebee gravity by constructing the generalized off-shell Gibbs free-energy landscape in the canonical ensemble at fixed effective pressure. We find analytically that the minimum temperature \(T_{\min}\) is independent of the Lorentz-violating parameter \(\alpha\), whereas the Hawking--Page temperature \(T_{\mathrm{HP}}\) increases monotonically with \(\alpha\). Consequently, the locally stable but globally disfavored large-black-hole window \(T_{\min}<T<T_{\mathrm{HP}}\) broadens with increasing \(\alpha\). Within the off-shell framework, we derive closed-form expressions for the global-preference gap \(\Delta G_{\mathrm{glob}}\), which measures the free-energy difference between the large-black-hole minimum and thermal AdS, and the barrier height \(\Delta G_{\mathrm{bar}}\), which measures the separation between the small-black-hole saddle and the large-black-hole minimum. We recover the Schwarzschild--AdS limit as \(\alpha\to0\). These results establish the off-shell free-energy landscape as a precise thermodynamic framework for diagnosing Lorentz-violating effects in AdS black-hole phase structure.

item.title: Thermodynamic compatibility, holographic property and wave-function representation of generalized weakly nonlocal self-gravitating non-relativistic fluids
item.description: arXiv:2504.07296v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two pillars of physics---gravity and quantum mechanics---are usually formulated in entirely separate languages. Surprisingly, both can be expressed in the language of a fluid: a self-gravitating fluid for Newtonian gravity, and a quantum-pressure-carrying fluid for the Schr\"odinger equation. In this work we show that this resemblance can be understood within a common framework based on how the Second Law of Thermodynamics constrains the class of non-dissipative continua considered here. Using a transparent thermodynamic procedure, we derive the most general fluid model within a chosen constitutive state space involving density, velocity, energy, an internal scalar field, and their spatial gradients. The framework recovers, as special cases, the Euler equations, a restricted family of Korteweg fluids (including the hydrodynamic form of the Schr\"odinger and Gross--Pitaevskii equations), Newtonian self-gravitating fluids, and the Schr\"odinger--Newton system. We identify the conditions under which perfect fluids exhibit \emph{classical holography}: the pressure-tensor divergence can then be represented by the gradient of a scalar potential. Classical holography yields a vorticity transport law that preserves sufficiently regular, initially irrotational flows and, under additional assumptions, enables a single complex-valued Schr\"odinger-like representation. While gravitational and quantum-hydrodynamic theories were investigated separately in our previous works, the present study develops a substantially more general scalar-internal-variable construction, refines its perfect-fluid analysis, and systematically embeds the earlier models within a unified framework. The framework also identifies a thermodynamically admissible density--gravity coupling that connects classical and quantum self-gravitating fluids, although its stability, and observational consequences remain to be explored.

item.title: On the nature of the black hole information problem
item.description: arXiv:2505.17220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this work is to present the black hole information problem and discuss the assumptions and hypotheses necessary for its formulation. As the problem arises in the framework of semiclassical gravity, we first review the necessary notions to describe Lorentzian manifolds equipped with physical properties, as well as the physical concepts of the theory that describes the gravitational interaction as the curvature of spacetime, general relativity. From its classical perspective, we develop the formalism to study the dynamical aspects of black holes in spacetimes obeying suitable causality conditions. Equipped with conjectures that nature censors naked singularities and that black holes reach a stationary configuration after they form, the black hole uniqueness theorems allow us to review several relations for the geometrical quantities associated with them. Following considerations of the other fundamental interactions, which are described by quantum field theory, we review the arguments in the formalism of quantum field theory in curved spacetime that give rise to the effective particle creation effect, its approximately thermal character, and the concept of black hole evaporation. With a precise quantification of information in quantum mechanics and assuming that the condition for physically acceptable states is given by the Hadamard condition, we review the result that entanglement between causally complementary regions is an intrinsic feature of quantum field theory. As a consequence, we discuss how the formation and complete evaporation of black holes leads to information loss. Conscious that such a prediction follows if no deviations from the semiclassical picture occur at the Planck scale, we discuss alternatives to this nonunitary dynamical evolution and formulate the black hole information problem. Lastly, we analyze the assumptions and hypotheses that lead to the problem.

item.title: Cosmological and High Energy Physics implications from gravitational-wave background searches in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's O1-O4a runs
item.description: arXiv:2510.26848v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We search for gravitational-wave background signals produced by various early Universe processes in the Advanced LIGO O4a dataset, combined with the data from the earlier O1, O2, and O3 (LIGO-Virgo) runs. The absence of detectable signals enables powerful constraints on fundamental physics. We derive gravitational-wave background energy density upper limits from the O1-O4a data to constrain parameters associated with various possible processes in the early Universe: first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings, domain walls, stiff equation of state, axion inflation, second-order scalar perturbations, primordial black hole binaries, and parity violation. In our analyses, the presence of an astrophysical background produced by compact (black hole and neutron star) binary coalescences throughout the Universe is also considered. We address the implications for various cosmological and high energy physics models based on the obtained parameter constraints. We conclude that LIGO-Virgo data already yield significant constraints on numerous early Universe scenarios.

item.title: Impact of a third body on binary neutron star tidal interactions
item.description: arXiv:2511.00621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To model a compact binary coalescence, it is commonly assumed that the binary evolves in isolation. In the present work, we relax this assumption by introducing a distant third body and investigate how the third body would affect the binary evolution. We treat this problem perturbatively and study tidal interaction in the binary due to the third body's presence. We introduce appropriate modifications to the equations governing the orbital motions and the evolution equations of the binary component's quadrupole moment. We compute the radiated energy and accumulated dephasing for the binary. Our findings indicate that for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects would not be significant. However, for binaries such as intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects are more relevant, and in some scenarios the accumulated dephasing can reach up to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radians.
