item.title: Cosmological Inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_{m})$ Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2511.09031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cosmological inflation provides the standard description of the early accelerated expansion of the Universe, but the shortcomings of General Relativity (GR) motivate the search for alternative gravitational frameworks. In this paper, we study inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity, constructed in the symmetric teleparallel formulation, where the non-metricity scalar $Q$ couples non-minimally to the matter Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_m$. We consider an inflaton scalar field with a power-law potential and show that, in this framework, the inflationary dynamics is governed by the interplay between the scalar field and the effective geometric sector generated by the matter-geometry coupling. Thus, the scalar field supplies the matter source, while the modified $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ structure alters the background evolution and the inflationary observables. Within the slow-roll approximation, we derive the expressions of the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for both linear and nonlinear coupling models. The linear model, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)=-\alpha Q+2\mathcal{L}_m+\beta$, is treated as a benchmark GR-like limit, whereas the nonlinear model, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)=-\alpha Q+(2\mathcal{L}_m)^2+\beta$, captures the genuinely modified effects of the theory. We find that the linear model remains consistent with the latest joint Planck 2018 and BICEP/Keck (BK18) constraints ($r < 0.036$ at $95\%$ CL) for positive $\alpha$ and $\beta$, while the nonlinear model is favored for negative values of these parameters and yields predictions largely concentrated within the $68\%$ confidence level. These results indicate that the nonlinear matter-geometry coupling can lead to distinct inflationary behavior and may improve the observational compatibility of the quadratic potential $(n=2)$, which is strongly disfavored in the standard GR-based inflationary scenario.
item.dc:creator: Maryam Shiravand, Saeed Fakhry, Javad T. Firouzjaee, Ali Tizfahm

item.title: Observational constraints on viscous free-$\gamma$ fluid in $f(Q)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2602.16757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the late-time cosmological dynamics of a spatially flat FLRW Universe in the framework of exponential $f(Q)$ gravity, where $Q$ denotes the nonmetricity scalar. The matter sector is described by a bulk viscous fluid with a generalized barotropic equation of state characterized by a free parameter $\gamma$, extending the standard pressureless matter scenario. We derive the modified background evolution equations and investigate the resulting cosmological dynamics. The model parameters are constrained using a combination of cosmic chronometer (CC), DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), CMB, and Type Ia supernova observations. Using the best-fit parameters, we analyze the phase-space dynamics of the model and employ the statefinder and $\mathrm{Om}(z)$ diagnostics to quantify deviations from the standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. We further examine the evolution of the deceleration parameter and the effective equation-of-state parameter, demonstrating a transition from an early matter-dominated decelerating epoch to the present phase of accelerated expansion. Overall, the model provides a viable framework for late-time cosmic acceleration, recovering the standard matter-dominated evolution at early times while naturally evolving toward a stable late-time de Sitter attractor consistent with current observations.

item.title: The point-particle-limit effective-source approach for computing gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge
item.description: arXiv:2603.27284v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The traditional effective-source method is hampered by complex analytical expressions and the inherent smoothness limit, which incur high computational costs and complicate implementation. To overcome these limitations, we introduce the point-particle-limit effective source method, which analytically takes the size of the effective source to zero, thereby transforming the problem into a well-defined jump condition of retarded metric field at the particle position governed by the local singular field. This formulation naturally pairs with a discontinuous Galerkin scheme, whose inherent capacity for accommodating solution discontinuities enables highly accurate enforcement of the jump conditions. We apply both the traditional and point-particle-limit effective source method to calculate the time-domain gravitational metric perturbation and gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge on a point particle in a circular orbit around a Schwarzschild black hole. The comparison of numerical results shows the excellent advantage of the point-particle-limit effective source method, which validates the correctness and efficiency of the point-particle-limit effective source method and thereby establishes a numerical foundation for computing generic geodesic orbits or long-time self-consistent orbital evolution.

item.title: Photon rings and shadows of black holes with non-minimal couplings between curvature and electromagnetic field
item.description:
arXiv:2604.16551v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate black holes with non-minimal couplings between the electromagnetic field and spacetime curvature tensors, focusing on their event horizons, shadows, and photon rings. Such couplings can naturally arise from effective field theories of gravity and quantum corrections in curved spacetime. Starting from a general action with three independent coupling terms, we derive static and spherically symmetric black hole solutions using a series expansion method. We find that all couplings enlarge the event horizon and photon sphere, while their observational consequences differ. The coupling $F^\mu_{\

item.title: Gravitational Light Deflection: Geometrical Methods and Nonlinear Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.17355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gravitational lensing constitutes one of the most direct observational manifestations of spacetime curvature and provides a powerful probe of compact astrophysical objects. In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of the bending of light in curved spacetime, beginning with the fundamental aspects of gravitational lensing and the Newtonian approximation to light deflection. The relativistic formulation of lensing is then developed through the lens equation, lensing potential, and a geometrical interpretation of Fermat's principle using an effective refractive index in curved spacetime. Photon trajectories and light deflection are subsequently investigated in static, spherically symmetric geometries, followed by a detailed study of photon motion in the equatorial plane of the Kerr spacetime. Analytical expressions for the closest approach distance and critical parameters governing photon orbits are derived. Furthermore, the bending angle is examined using the Rindler-Ishak method and the Gauss-Bonnet theorem within the optical geometry. Finally, the analysis is extended to axisymmetric spacetimes using the OIA and GW-OIA formalisms, providing a unified geometrical framework for computing light deflection in both static and rotating gravitational fields. The review also examines nonlinear electrodynamics (NED), distinguishing changes in the gravitational background from changes in the characteristic propagation of electromagnetic waves. Representative models are used to relate these effects to finite-distance deflection, polarization-dependent optical observables, and comparisons between weak bending and strong-field capture.

item.title: Radiation properties of a regular black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo with a thin accretion disk
item.description: arXiv:2604.21615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the shadow, timelike geodesic structure, and thin accretion disk radiation properties of a static spherically symmetric regular black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo. Using the EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A*, we constrain the halo scale parameter $a$ at $1\sigma$ and $2\sigma$ levels. Based on the Page--Thorne model and a backward ray-tracing method, we compute the local radiative flux, redshift factor distribution, and observed flux images for different viewing angles. We further compare the Dehnen regular black hole with the Einasto and Hayward regular black holes by evaluating their ISCO radii and disk flux profiles. The results show that increasing $a$ reduces the ISCO radius, enlarges the effective radiation area, and amplifies the Doppler asymmetry of both direct and secondary images. Compared with the Einasto and Hayward models, the Dehnen black hole exhibits the strongest ISCO contraction and the most pronounced left-right brightness asymmetry, while the Einasto model is nearly insensitive to its scale parameter and the Hayward black hole shows only a mild dependence. These findings demonstrate that regular black holes with different regularisation mechanisms can be distinguished by their accretion disk images, providing a potential tool for testing dark-matter halo models with future high-resolution observations.

item.title: Natural modification of quantum uncertainty, modified gravity, and cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2605.18203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A common approach in physics and mathematics is to extend and modify theories and frameworks by considering what is often described as a `natural' extension or modification by including higher-order terms or by introducing other non-linearities. We show that such an approach must be taken with care as physical models can be connected in indirect ways. What looks like a natural approach in one setting will likely not be natural in another. We use the flat Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker equations of cosmology to connect the generalized uncertainty principle to modified theories of gravity. A simple additional term in one setting leads to enormous complications in the other. We identify Born-Infeld models as the only ones which appear natural in both settings.

item.title: Frenet--Serret invariants of timelike worldlines in Kerr spacetime: chart independence, horizon crossing and null-endpoint limits
item.description: arXiv:2605.29759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine the Frenet-Serret (FS) curvature kappa and first torsion tau_1 of timelike worldlines in Kerr spacetime, focusing mainly on non-Killing equatorial trajectories. Since these quantities are scalars associated with a worldline, a coordinate transformation cannot remove a divergence for the same curve. We demonstrate this by transforming a single worldline between five coordinate charts and verifying agreement of its invariants, including in an off-equatorial test. We also show why reusing the same coordinate components of the tangent vector in two charts generally describes different curves. For a non-unit tangent v with norm S = g(v,v), we derive the identity kappa squared = Q squared / S cubed - (q dot q) / S squared, where q = nabla_v v and Q = q dot v. When Q approaches a nonzero limit and q dot q remains finite, the curvature scales as |Q_0| S to the power -3/2 as the curve approaches a null endpoint. Under the additional condition that S' is nonzero, we obtain a closed expression for the limiting value of tau_1. We verify these results using exact symbolic calculations for two Kerr-Schild spirals, including one with spin parameter a greater than the mass M, for which no event horizon exists. For Killing observers, we derive closed-form expressions for kappa and tau_1 and show that both become singular at light surfaces. Finally, we distinguish FS torsion, which measures rotation relative to the acceleration direction, from gyroscope rotation rates defined using regular reference frames. For a geodesic plunge, the rotation rate relative to the principal-null frame remains finite across the horizon, while the rate relative to the Carter-plane axis agrees with Marck's precession rate. Our analysis focuses mainly on equatorial examples; a numerical comparison in double-null coordinates is left for future work.
item.dc:creator: Paulami Majumder

item.title: Quantum Reference Fields Transformations in Linearized Quantum Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.09344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffeomorphism invariance is a central feature of general relativity. Without external reference structures, matter and geometry must be specified relationally, with respect to internal subsystems serving as reference frames. In quantum gravity, these reference systems must themselves be treated as quantum, motivating the use of quantum reference frames. In this work, we address how such a relational description could be formulated within linearized quantum gravity. To this purpose, we introduce quantum reference fields, i.e.,sets of four dynamical scalar fields whose stress-energy tensors enter the gravitational constraints. These fields extend the notion of quantum reference frames to local field-theoretic reference systems, allowing matter and gravitational degrees of freedom to be described relationally with respect to physical quantum systems whose states cannot be sharply peaked on definite field configurations. By generalizing the perspective-neutral construction of quantum reference frames, we show that relational, gauge invariant observables admit reduced descriptions in the perspective of each quantum reference field, and we derive the unitary transformations relating them. The resulting unitary maps implement local quantum coordinate changes between different internal perspectives, and act on the linearized gravitational field with an analogous structure to a linearized diffeomorphism, but with the classical gauge parameter replaced by a physical quantum field. Finally, we construct a relational von Neumann-type measurement scheme, showing how the corresponding reduced observables can be accessed operationally from the perspective of a quantum reference field.
item.dc:creator: Lin-Qing Chen, Flaminia Giacomini

item.title: Sensing the Inflationary Production of Scalars
item.description: arXiv:2606.17963v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review the mechanism by which loops of matter fields contribute to the graviton self-energy during de Sitter inflation. This self-energy is used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equations. A Green's function method is employed to obtain exact 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, subject to the usual ambiguity in the initial state. Conformally coupled matter, which does not experience inflationary particle production, makes only a logarithmic enhancement of the rate at which the imaginary part of the mode function goes to zero after horizon crossing. These corrections can be understood, and even summed up, using a variant of the renormalization group. However, massless, minimally coupled scalars, which experience massive inflationary particle production, induce a much stronger enhancement of the rate at which the real part of the mode function approaches a constant. One interpretation of this effect is as a shift of the inflationary Hubble parameter.
item.dc:creator: A. J. Foraci, C. Litos, R. P. Woodard

item.title: Population-level correlations in Bayesian statistics: an illustrative model for gravitational-wave astronomy
item.description: arXiv:2606.21076v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With increasingly large numbers of gravitational-wave events, population inference is now beginning to move beyond predictions of marginal distributions and to probe correlations between compact-binary parameters such as masses, spins, and redshifts. These correlations have strong constraining power for both astrophysics and tests of general relativity. In this paper, we present an idealized analytical model to study the interplay between single-event correlations, systematic biases, and population-level correlations. With this, we investigate the potential emergence of false-positive measurements of population-level correlations. We quantify how the presence of correlations at the single-event level between a pair of parameters increases the uncertainty of population-level correlations for those parameters, potentially obscuring the true underlying population correlation if present. We also find that if waveform systematics lead to biases that are correlated across the catalog (which is likely, because certain regions of the parameter space are more difficult to model), this can be effectively absorbed by a population analysis that targets correlations and can be misinterpreted as such. This simple Gaussian-based model may serve as a broad compass for future, more detailed explorations.
item.dc:creator: Caroline B. Owen, Alexandre Toubiana, Davide Gerosa

item.title: Time-domain framework for the Teukolsky equation with a particle source using comoving hyperboloidal coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2606.26339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a scheme and implementation code for time-domain integration of the Teukolsky equation in 1+1 dimensions with a point-particle source, based on comoving, spatially compactified hyperboloidal coordinates. We demonstrate that the scheme evades the problem of nonphysical growing modes that plague some numerical evolution schemes without compactification. Our use of comoving coordinates greatly simplifies the application of jump conditions on the particle's worldline. We develop our method and test its performance for a scalar field on a Schwarzschild background, first for a circular geodesic orbit source and then for a scattering geodesic orbit. We then present a test implementation of the method for the $s = -2$ Teukolsky equation, illustrating its long-term stability and absence of growing-mode behavior through comparison with similar results using noncompactified characteristic coordinates. Our method paves the way to calculations of the full gravitational self-force in extreme-mass-ratio scattering.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Vaswani, Leor Barack, Oliver Long, Rodrigo Panosso Macedo

item.title: Massive boson stars: Waveform-based branch diagnosis with neural reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2606.26436v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate whether the dynamical merger branch of massive boson-star collisions can be inferred from the gravitational waveform without supplying the intrinsic source parameters. Using an existing equal-mass, head-on numerical-relativity catalogue, we construct branch-conditioned reduced-basis surrogates for the real $(2,0)$ and $(4,0)$ modes and perform parameter-blind waveform inference. On a frozen test set of 60 held-out samples, the correct branch is recovered for all samples using either mode, showing that the branch information is not confined to the dominant $(2,0)$ channel. The inference also recovers $|\phi_c|$ with a mean relative error of $4.30\%$ and selects the correct $\lambda$ from $\{10,50,100,300\}$ in $68.3\%$ of the test samples. These results demonstrate waveform-based branch and source-parameter inference within the present noiseless numerical-relativity catalogue.
item.dc:creator: Bo-Xuan Ge

item.title: A Starobinsky-like Potential in k-Essence Framework: Attractor Dynamics, Reheating, and Consistency with ACT DR6
item.description: arXiv:2607.06112v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recent ACT DR6 has shifted the preferred value of the scalar spectral index upward so that many well-established inflationary models have been disfavoured, including the Starobinsky potential. Despite this, the Starobinsky potential remains exceptionally well-motivated, with origins in $R^2$ gravity, no-scale supergravity, and the $\alpha$-attractor framework. In this work, we show that the Starobinsky potential can be fully revived within a k-essence framework, described by the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L} = F(\phi)X - V(\phi)$, with a power-law kinetic coupling $F(\phi) = 1+A\phi^n$ and no modification to the gravitational sector. Solving the background equations numerically, we find that the predictions for $n_s$, $\alpha_s$, and $r$ fall within the $1\sigma$ region of ACT DR6 for a well-defined range of the coupling parameters. The attractor behavior of the inflationary solution is confirmed both analytically through the Hamilton-Jacobi formalism and numerically via a phase-space analysis. For the reheating phase, it is discussed that due to the nature of the Starobinsky potential, the effective equation of state parameter is fixed as $w_{\rm re} = 0$, resulting in a reheating temperature $T_{\rm re} \sim 10^{14}~{\rm GeV}$, well above the BBN bound. The relic gravitational wave spectrum is also computed and it is found that they can lie within the sensitivity bound of the BBO. These results demonstrate that the Starobinsky potential remains a theoretically viable candidate for inflation and that its incompatibility with ACT DR6 in the canonical setting can be resolved by introducing a simple non-canonical kinetic coupling without any modification to the underlying gravitational theory.
item.dc:creator: Abolhassan Mohammadi, Yogesh, Hongwei Tan, M. Sami

item.title: Modified Cosmology from Mass-to-Horizon Relation: Observational Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2607.18521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We constrain the class of modified cosmologies derived in Paper I [1] from a generalized mass-to-horizon relation (MHR) that enforces thermodynamic consistency between the Cai-Kim horizon temperature and generalized horizon entropies. The modified Friedmann equations depend on an entropy exponent $m$, an MHR coupling parameter $\gamma$, and an entanglement-correction amplitude $f_B$, with standard $\Lambda$CDM recovered in the appropriate limit. Using Pantheon$+$/SH0ES Type~Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, we constrain eight physically motivated sub-cases via Markov chain Monte Carlo and compare models through the Bayesian log-evidence. The entropy exponent is tightly bounded, $|m-1|\lesssim O(10^{-4})$ when the MHR coupling is fixed ($\gamma=1$), relaxing to $O(10^{-3})$ along the $m$-$\gamma$ degeneracy, excluding any macroscopically significant departure from standard horizon thermodynamics. Freeing the MHR coupling parameter or the entanglement amplitude raises the inferred Hubble constant to $h\simeq0.70$-$0.71$, reducing the CMB-SH0ES tension from ${\sim}4\sigma$ to ${\sim}1.2$-$2.6\sigma$, but no scenario fully resolves it within a flat universe. The Bayesian log-evidence nevertheless disfavors every extension relative to $\Lambda$CDM in all dataset combinations ($-16\lesssim\Delta\ln Z \lesssim-1$): the improved fits obtained when the SH0ES calibration is included reflect an absorption of the Hubble tension by the additional parameters rather than genuine evidence for modified horizon entropy.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Prasanthan, Hussain Gohar, Vincenzo Salzano

item.title: Taub-NUT as gravitational dyon with torsion
item.description: arXiv:2607.25654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the Levi-Civita connection for the Taub-NUT metric is singular on Misner strings and generates an Einstein tensor containing the squares of the delta function. This can be improved by introducing torsion, in which case the Einstein tensor may be interpreted as that of a cosmic string with negative variable tension. Komar flows in Misner strings are generated by torsion, which is therefore responsible for the asymptotic Komar charges. The Taub-NUT metric then appears as a soliton supported by two spin-fluid beams.
item.dc:creator: Dmitri Gal'tsov, Rostom Karsanov

item.title: Exact solutions for static spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid in Rastall theory
item.description: arXiv:2607.26463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In general relativity, exact Liouvillian solutions for a static and spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid and the equation of state $p(r)=w\rho (r)$ are known only for $w=0,-\frac{1}{6}, -\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{1}{3}$, and $-1$. We extend this setup to Rastall theory, presenting the relation between the Rastall parameter and the constant $w$, and deriving exact solutions that correspond to their known counterparts in general relativity, except for $w=-\frac{1}{6}$. Furthermore, we find that, when $w\neq \frac{1}{3}, -1$, there exist several types of solutions whose behaviors change depending on the choice of constants.
item.dc:creator: Yoshimune Tomikawa, Ichika Obara, Takumi Orimo

item.title: Discrete symmetries of modified Teukolsky equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.27053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Teukolsky equation possesses discrete symmetries that constrain the properties of black hole perturbations and their quasinormal mode spectrum. In this study, we explore how a class of modifications of the Teukolsky potential can alter the symmetry structure of the equation and break the m = 0 degeneracy of quasinormal modes. We prove this result in frequency domain using the master Teukolsky equation and in time domain via (2+1)-dimensional simulations. We also show that the discrete symmetries can be leveraged for a more efficient characterization of the m = 0 quasinormal modes from time-domain evolutions. As a theory-specific application, we consider the case of higher-derivative theories of gravity, highlighting that time-domain implementations of frequency-domain potentials can give rise to additional non-physical branches of modes.
item.dc:creator: Ciro De Simone

item.title: Global hyperbolicity meets order completeness
item.description: arXiv:2608.03476v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, an order completeness property has attracted attention in some low regularity spacetime geometry literature, where it was named `chronocompleteness'. In this work we prove that, in the framework of standard Lorentzian geometry, this property is equivalent to global hyperbolicity. The equivalence of global hyperbolicity with other more traditional forms of order completeness is also established.
item.dc:creator: E. Minguzzi

item.title: The Bondi dipole in full numerical relativity: a self-accelerating positive-negative mass binary
item.description: arXiv:2608.24577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bondi showed in 1957 that a body of negative active gravitational mass and a positive one should accelerate together without limit while their total momentum stays zero. We test this prediction in full 3+1 numerical relativity, from constraint-satisfying initial data. The matter is two complex scalar fields with identical self-interactions, one of which enters the Einstein equations with the opposite sign; its stars have positive inertial and passive masses but negative active and Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) masses. To our knowledge, they are the first asymptotically flat bodies of negative ADM mass evolved in numerical relativity. A pair of stars with equal and opposite ADM masses accelerates as a single object at constant separation, and its total momentum stays zero to within 0.5%. The acceleration follows Newton's law of gravitation in both mass and separation, reverses when the stars are exchanged, and is absent in same-sign pairs and isolated stars. We detect no gravitational radiation. The results hold for head-on pairs released from rest, up to a few percent of the speed of light, and in the longest run the pair reaches a tenth of it with both stars intact.
item.dc:creator: Nikita M. Shirokov, Ilya Nachevsky

item.title: NRHJSur3dq8: a spectral numerical-relativity surrogate family for non-eccentric aligned-spin binary-black-hole waveforms
item.description: arXiv:2609.09088v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present NRHJSur3dq8, a family of numerical-relativity surrogates for non-eccentric aligned-spin binary-black-hole waveforms inspired by an action-angle parameterization. The model provides both the dynamics: the Hamiltonian values, azimuthal action $J_\phi(\Phi)$, the orbital clock $\tau(\Phi)$ as functions of its phasing, and the radiative pieces: the waveforms, their near-analytic derivatives, and modeling errors associated with each. The surrogated variables are conditioned into pieces that vary slowly on the radiation-reaction timescale, represented on shared $h$-adaptive Chebyshev elements, and regressed across the intrinsic parameters with a Gaussian-process model. A time-parameterized merger-ringdown set of elements is attached where the adiabatic description breaks down. Fixed-hyperparameter leave-one-out validation of the central NRHJSur3dq8_AA model variant against numerical relativity gives a $(2,2)$ unweighted mismatch of $1.6^{+62}_{-1.5}\times10^{-6}$ and an all-mode mismatch of $2.8^{+84}_{-2.7}\times10^{-6}$ over the full inspiral-merger-ringdown span. Sky-averaged and signal-to-noise-ratio-weighted over $32$ orientations per simulation, the model's full inspiral-merger-ringdown in-sample mismatch against the SXS numerical-relativity simulations used for training is $8.9\times10^{-7}$ to $2.8\times10^{-5}$ across total masses $40$-$120 M_\odot$. Waveforms are hybridized using post-Newtonian waveforms. Beyond accuracy, NRHJSur3dq8 provides two capabilities uncommon in numerical-relativity surrogates: nearly analytic derivatives of the strain with respect to the physical parameters, and a calibrated Gaussian-process predictive uncertainty of the model. A full non-hybridized inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform evaluates in $12.5$ ms on a single CPU call. Batched evaluation takes $0.43$ ms per waveform at a batch of $4096$, measured at a starting frequency of $25$ Hz.
item.dc:creator: Vaishak Prasad

item.title: Black Hole Spacetime Reconstruction from Galactic Rotation Curves: Thermodynamic Properties and Implications
item.description: arXiv:2609.17570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the dark-matter environment of a galaxy, reconstructed directly from its observed rotation curve, affects the black hole at its centre. Using the rotation curve of the spiral galaxy NGC\,5907, we construct a general-relativistic model of its halo. The halo has a positive, outward-decreasing density, satisfies the null energy condition, and reproduces the galaxy's dynamical mass of about $3.3\times10^{11}M_\odot$ within 30\,kpc. We then embed a central black hole in this halo and derive its horizon, Hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, photon sphere and shadow. Because the halo's gravitational field is weak, all these quantities differ from those of an isolated Schwarzschild black hole by less than one part in $10^{5}$. The heat capacity remains negative, so the black hole stays thermodynamically unstable. For a black hole of $10^{8}M_\odot$, the shadow would span about 0.6\,microarcseconds. Archival WISE infrared photometry confirms, as expected, that the black hole leaves no imprint on the galaxy's light on kiloparsec scales.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Sanyal, Farook Rahaman

item.title: Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.13206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present what are, to our knowledge, the first three-dimensional numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes held open by a phantom scalar field, whose energy density is nowhere positive. We construct constraint-satisfying initial data for single throats and for pairs, at rest and with orbital momentum, and evolve them with adaptive mesh refinement. An isolated throat is unstable: depending on the sign of a small perturbation, it collapses to a black hole or inflates, at the rate that linear perturbation theory predicts to within 1.9%. Two throats at rest repel when their scalar charges have the same sign and attract when the signs are opposite, with a strength ratio close to the scalar force law's prediction, so only opposite-signed pairs merge. A head-on collision forms a common horizon around both throats while they are still open. The horizon then loses 28% of its area as it absorbs the scalar field, and approaches the Schwarzschild radius of the pair's mass. Pairs that fly past each other form no horizon, and both throats inflate. Every encounter emits a short burst of gravitational waves and a scalar dipole wave of comparable, negative energy. An isolated collapsing throat rings at the quasinormal frequency of the black hole it becomes. No throat survives more than a few orbital periods, even when its initial perturbation is tiny, so these binaries do not inspiral. The results hold for one phantom-scalar model, equal masses, a single throat compactness and no spin.
item.dc:creator: Nikita M. Shirokov, Ilya Nachevsky

item.title: Strong Field Gravitational Lensing in Full Wave Optics
item.description: arXiv:2610.18958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compact binaries evolving in the vicinity of massive black holes may be commonplace in the Universe, and their gravitational waves carry signatures of their environment. We study the strong lensing of these signals by the massive companion, a configuration that violates the standard assumptions of the lensing literature: geometric optics and thin lenses. Using a perturbative framework, we compute the full wave optics amplification factors for face-on and edge-on binaries, including spinning lenses. In the edge-on configuration, peak amplification does not occur at perfect source--lens--observer alignment, even for a non-spinning lens. This is a consequence of the anisotropic, coherent quadrupolar emission of the stellar-mass binary breaking the axisymmetry of the system. Restricting to the equatorial plane near the optical axis, we then find that the frequency dependence of the amplification factor is universal across every configuration studied, persisting deep into the wave optics regime. Comparing against a strong-field ray tracing calculation, we find agreement at the $\sim10\%$ level for a face-on binary lensed by a Schwarzschild black hole. In the less symmetric edge-on case only the angular peak shift and fringe spacing is reproduced to this accuracy. For a Kerr lens, the face-on amplification factor is described by its Schwarzschild counterpart to the same $\sim 10 \%$ accuracy once the effect of frame dragging is corrected for. A point mass lens, by contrast, fails to reproduce the features of the system, which may have strong implications for forecasts that adopt it for lensing by massive black holes in the strong field.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao S. Santos, Luka Vujeva

item.title: Strong-Field Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Ray-Traced Arrival-Time Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. However, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. In particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). We present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the Hamilton--Jacobi equations. In doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. For a stationary source at $10M$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. Furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 M$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. This work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6M \to \infty$. It provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.
item.dc:creator: Luka Vujeva, Jo\~ao S. Santos, Brian C. Seymour

item.title: Black holes in thermal bath live shorter: Implications for primordial black holes
item.description: arXiv:2501.11925v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hawking radiation from a non-extremal black hole is known to be approximately Planckian. The thermal spectrum receives multiple corrections including greybody factors and due to kinematical restrictions on the infrared and ultraviolet frequencies. We show that another significant correction to the spectrum arises if the black hole is assumed to live in a thermal bath and the emitted radiation gets thermalised at the bath temperature. This modification reshapes the thermal spectrum, and leads to appreciable deviation from standard results including modification in the decay rate of black holes. We argue that this altered decay rate has significance for cosmology and, in a realistic setting, show that it alters the life time of primordial black holes (PBHs) in the early universe. In particular, the very light PBHs formed right after the end of inflation decay faster which may have interesting phenomenological implications.
item.dc:creator: Jitumani Kalita, Debaprasad Maity, Ayan Chatterjee

item.title: BV Pushforward of Palatini-Cartan gravity
item.description: arXiv:2507.06279v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The goal of this note is to show that the standard BV formulation of gravity in the Palatini-Cartan formalism is equivalent, using a BV pushforward, to an AKSZ-like version compatible with BFV data on the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Canepa, Alberto S. Cattaneo

item.title: One-sided Witnesses for the Quantumness of Gravitational Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2507.15588v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum information concepts and quantum technologies have opened the prospect of probing the quantum nature of gravity in table-top experiments. Most proposals rely on detecting gravitationally mediated entanglement, which requires measurements on both interacting systems. Here we propose an alternative test based on witnessing quantum memory effects in the dynamics of a single system. We show how the quantum memory concept allows the non-classicality of the interaction between two systems to be certified through local measurements on only one of them. We then develop a novel quantum memory witness, making the approach applicable to gravitationally coupled harmonic oscillators. This witness requires no assumptions about the dynamics, such as Gaussianity. Our results show that the quantumness of gravitational dynamics can be certified with access to only one subsystem, opening the door to asymmetric implementations that can offer conceptual and experimental advantages to probing the quantum nature of the gravitational interaction.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Beyer, M. S. Kim, Igor Pikovski

item.title: Topological cones and positively polarizable hyperbolic norms
item.description: arXiv:2508.17052v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the first part of this article, we study linear cones over totally ordered fields. We show that for each such cone there uniquely exists a universal vector space (called its spanned vector space) into which it embeds as a generating convex cone. Moreover, we investigate topologies on cones for which the natural cone operations are continuous, and study how these topologies carry over to the spanned vector space. In the second part, we deal with hyperbolic norms which satisfy a polarization identity and are defined on cones over the real numbers. We show that, under reasonable assumptions, such hyperbolic norms induce a Lorentzian inner product on the spanned vector space. Finally, we establish a link between completeness under the Wick rotation of a Lorentzian inner product and order-theoretic completeness.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Kharitonov, Argam Ohanyan

item.title: Charged Black-Hole Binary Evolution at Second Post-Newtonian Order
item.description: arXiv:2509.20432v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the dynamics of electrically charged black-hole binaries and their gravitational-wave emission during the inspiral phase. Within the post-Newtonian framework, we derive the conservative and dissipative dynamics up to second order (2PN), combining Effective Field Theory and classical methods. We compute the NNLO conservative Lagrangian, LO dissipative effects in harmonic and Lorenz gauges, and provide the equations of motion, center-of-mass transformations, and the Lagrangian/Hamiltonian in ADM-type coordinates. We also obtain gauge-invariant expressions for the binding energy, periastron advance in quasi-circular orbits, and the scattering angle in unbound orbits. Our results extend previous analyses and are fully consistent with recent post-Minkowskian findings.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Placidi, Elisa Grilli, Marta Orselli, Matteo Pegorin, Nicola Bartolo, Pierpaolo Mastrolia

item.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
item.description: arXiv:2512.24233v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Analogue gravity describes sound as a field propagating on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, which is usually treated as given; in reality, however, quantum fluctuations also feed back on the medium that defines this spacetime. This raises the question of whether a condensate modified by this backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field, which has not been established so far. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, which keeps the classical background and the quantum fluctuation distinct while retaining their mutual coupling, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation still propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate, but is no longer massless: it obeys a Klein-Gordon equation with a spacetime-dependent mass that is generated by the backreaction sources in the continuity and Euler equations and cannot be absorbed into the metric. Backreaction in a Bose-Einstein condensate is thus a change of the analogue spacetime, supplemented by a mass term that has no geometric counterpart. Solving the coupled condensate-Bogoliubov dynamics for a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas quenched from a noninteracting state, we find that, while the depletion remains below $2\%$, backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered equal-point phase correlation by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to about $20\%$ near the walls, and that the bulk enhancement survives a finite-resolution imaging model.
item.dc:creator: Sang-Shin Baak, Hyun-Yong Lee

item.title: Bulk Phase Shift and Singularity
item.description: arXiv:2602.06558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-energy scattering of a light particle off a black hole at fixed impact parameter is described by an eikonal phase, which encodes the resulting time delay and angular deflection. This bulk phase shift admits a holographic interpretation as of the thermal momentum-space two-point function of a scalar operator in the CFT in the Regge limit. At small impact parameter, the phase shift acquires an imaginary part signaling inelastic scattering, obscuring the interpretation of time delay and deflection which become complex-valued. However, in a holographic CFT these quantities can also be extracted from the so called bulk-cone singularities of the position space thermal correlator. Extending this analysis to small impact parameters, we find that the position-space correlator develops a singularity precisely when a null geodesic reflects off the black hole singularity and reaches the opposite boundary. This provides a more robust identification of bulk time delay and angular deflection through singularities of position-space correlators.
item.dc:creator: Yueke Jia, Manuela Kulaxizi

item.title: Diffusive dark fluids with Planck-2018 and DESI BAO DR2 Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2603.02828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we constrain the diffusive dark fluid cosmological model, wherein energy is transferred between the two dark components through a diffusion process. We extended the work in Ref. \cite{sahlu2026observational} by employing Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data from the Planck 2018 measurements in combination with Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 (2024). From the results, we found that the discrepancies in \(H_0\) measurements are \(1.90\sigma\) and \(1.72\sigma\) between the Planck 2018 value \((H_0 = 67.4\pm0.5\ \mathrm{km,s^{-1},Mpc^{-1}})\) and our diffusive model values, \(H_0 = 67.27^{+0.54}_{-0.55}\;,\) and \(68.35^{+0.31}_{-0.29} \), respectively. We also observe that the effects of the interaction on cosmic evolution and structure formation; we emphasize this by computing the scale-dependent density contrast and the matter power spectrum, compared with the $\Lambda$CDM model.
item.dc:creator: Shambel Sahlu, Amare Abebe

item.title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
item.description: arXiv:2603.28857v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or `mountain' - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. In previous work, we showed that anisotropic heat transport in magnetised accreting neutron stars can source a significant temperature asymmetry, and made rough estimates that suggested temperature-induced perturbations in the pressure supplied by the crustal lattice may be competitive with the widely known model of temperature-induced capture-layer shifts. In this paper we carry out detailed calculations to properly explore this scenario. We self-consistently calculate the temperature asymmetries, the perturbations in crustal lattice pressure, and the mass asymmetries within a single framework. For the first time, we make use of the set of realistic equations of state from the Brussels-Montreal nuclear energy-density functionals BSk19, BSk20, and BSk21 which describe all regions of accreting neutron stars in a thermodynamically consistent, unified way. We find these mountains are too small to dictate the spin-equilibrium of LMXBs, and estimate the level of gravitational wave emission they produce.
item.dc:creator: T. J. Hutchins, D. I. Jones

item.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
item.description: arXiv:2604.15159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
item.dc:creator: Hari K. Kunduri, James Lucietti

item.title: Non-extensive entropy of Vinen quantum turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2604.19478v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In Ref. [1] the statistical structure of the turbulent cascade in the context of non-additive entropy was considered. Here we suggest that the vortex line ensemble in the Vinen quantum turbulence in superfluids is described by the non-extensive Tsallis-Cirto statistics with $\delta=3$. This in particular leads to the temperature, which describes the thermodynamics of the Vinen ensemble, $T\sim mv^2$, where $v$ is the velocity of the flow and $m$ is the mass of the atom of the superfluid liquid.
item.dc:creator: G. E. Volovik

item.title: Targeting black holes from metal-poor progenitors with next-generation gravitational-wave detectors
item.description: arXiv:2606.03776v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer will be able to detect binary black-hole mergers out to the cosmic dawn. Mergers observed in the local Universe represent a mixture of systems formed across the entire cosmic history, spanning a wide range of astrophysical environments. Iron-group elements govern metallicity effects on stellar evolution, making metallicity a key tracer that leaves a strong imprint on the black-hole population. We introduce the concept of a ``target'' redshift, $z_t$, defined as the epoch at which more than $90\%$ of stars form with metallicity $Z < 0.1\,Z_\odot$. This provides a straightforward way to isolate mergers originating from metal-poor environments. The determination of $z_t$ relies on the reconstruction of the cosmic star formation rate density as a function of iron abundance. This reconstruction is not unique, as it depends on the combination of different empirical scaling relations. Consequently, $z_t$ spans a broad range, from $z_t \sim 4$ to $z_t > 10$, depending on the adopted model variation. We present a statistical framework that enables rapid tests of astrophysical predictions against forecasted observations from next-generation \acrlong{gw} detectors. By quantifying variations in the binary black-hole merger-rate density between the target redshift and the local Universe, our approach maps evolutionary trends across parameter space and estimates the detection statistics required to distinguish genuine astrophysical variations from statistical fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Federico Leto di Priolo, Martyna Chru\'sli\'nska, Davide Gerosa

item.title: Logarithmic corrections to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in New Massive Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.13546v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the one-loop correction to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity at the special point where the theory exhibits a unique maximally symmetric vacuum and non-constant curvature hairy black holes can achieve extremality even in the static case. Focusing on the near-horizon AdS$_2\times S^1$ geometry, we evaluate the contribution of boundary graviton modes that become exact zero modes in the extremal limit. We show that the resulting one-loop partition function generates logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy, providing a new extension to higher-curvature gravity of what has been recently obtained for near-extremal black holes in General Relativity.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Acito, Mariano Chernicoff, Julio Oliva, Cielo Ramirez de Arellano Torres, Mat\'ias Sempe

item.title: Black hole thermodynamics and KK photon quantum corrections in 2D effective dilaton gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.14016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study black hole thermodynamics using a two-dimensional effective theory obtained by dimensional reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For spherically symmetric charged black holes, the resulting dilaton gravity has a nonlinear potential that reproduces the semiclassical phase structure of four-dimensional AdS black holes, including the Hawking--Page transition and the small/large Reissner--Nordstr\"{o}m--AdS black hole transition. This shows that the two-dimensional theory before taking the near-horizon and near-extremal limits captures non-extremal thermodynamics beyond the Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity regime. We also include electromagnetic Kaluza--Klein modes on the internal sphere and integrate them out to derive the one-loop effective dilaton gravity. At leading order in the derivative expansion, these corrections appear as constant shifts in the black hole entropy and in the effective charge parameter of the dilaton potential. Therefore, the semiclassical phase structure is not qualitatively modified within this leading local approximation.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi

item.title: Gravitational Compton scattering at the fourth post-Minkowskian order
item.description: arXiv:2606.28239v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the classical gravitational Compton amplitude at the fourth post-Minkowskian order, $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$, within the Worldline Quantum Field Theory framework. We derive the associated $N$-matrix element, which provides the gravitational-wave scattering phase shift at the same order. As a nontrivial check, we show that our result agrees with black-hole perturbation theory.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Brunello, Mario Meo, Sid Smith

item.title: A Covariance-Aware Framework for Spatially Resolved Exoplanet Biosignature Inference with the Solar Gravitational Lens
item.description: arXiv:2606.29138v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Assessing possible life on an exoplanet requires spatial, spectral, temporal, and environmental context. We develop a covariance-aware Solar Gravitational Lens (SGL) framework for regional biosignature inference from reconstructed Einstein-ring measurements. A controlled 0.45-2.40 um Stokes-$I$ experiment uses ten illuminated cells, 128 channels, and R=70 to compare resolved and exactly projected disk spectra with common parameters and priors. Across 96 synthetic scenes, the joint gas, vegetation, and mineral block gains (1.52+/-0.03) nats after marginalizing cloud and calibration/response parameters; adding independently trained surrogate-discrepancy covariance gives (1.49+/-0.03) nats. Held-out mismatch nevertheless produces linearized shifts up to 6.08 posterior standard deviations; preserved precision does not establish unbiased recovery or evidence for life. For fixed Gaussian hypotheses, the expected log-likelihood-ratio loss under disk integration equals half the squared whitened contrast discarded by the projection. A separate 0.40-20 um continuum calculation provides absolute photon rates and observing-time estimates for an Earth-radius planet at 30 pc, observed from 650 AU. It includes source-averaged SGL amplification, finite-aperture extraction, coronal and host-star photons, detector noise, and a declared calibration floor. A reconstruction-covariance bracket reduces an 8 x 8 coadd gain from 7.77 to 3.00, costing 6.7 times the exposure in the statistical-noise limit. The framework connects regional spectroscopy and co-location tests to the physical and instrumental validation needed to assess exoplanet biospheres and possible biological activity.
item.dc:creator: Slava G. Turyshev

item.title: Probing Graviton Mass with MeerKAT PTA and SKA-PTA Forecasts
item.description: arXiv:2607.14790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this study, we derive constraints on the graviton mass using the 4.5-year data release from the MeerKAT Pulsar Timing Array (MPTA) and provide forecasts for the upcoming Square Kilometre Array PTA (SKA-PTA). By modeling the modified dispersion relation and the corresponding tensor correlation function for massive gravitons, we perform Bayesian inference on the angular-correlation measurements under three noise configurations. Our 90\% credible upper limits on the graviton mass span $m_g < (2.10$-$2.58) \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$. Including monopolar and dipolar contributions does not significantly alter these bounds, confirming that the constraints are driven by the quadrupolar tensor correlation. All results remain fully consistent with general relativity. For SKA-PTA, we forecast sensitivities down to $m_g \sim 10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 10-year observing baseline and $m_g \sim 10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 50-year observing baseline, representing order-of-magnitude improvements over current limits. This work demonstrates the power of current and future PTA observations to test fundamental aspects of gravity in the nanohertz band.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Chao Zhao, Sai Wang

item.title: A Four-Dimensional Gaussian Random Field Generator for Modeling Spatiotemporal Variability in Astrophysical Sources
item.description: arXiv:2607.16576v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Semi-analytic models of black-hole movies require both an emitting flow prescription and a time-dependent source variability. Existing prescriptions are often limited to either equatorial emission or time-independent sources. In this work we present a unified model for these two ingredients. First, we prescribe an off-equatorial, nongeodesic Kerr fluid rotation law by lifting an equatorial specific-angular-momentum profile to cylindrical surfaces, setting the polar component of the four-velocity to zero, normalizing the flow with the full Kerr metric at the spacetime point, and retaining the option to recover a geodesic-like plunging prescription when needed. Second, we use this velocity as the disk advection field in a four-dimensional inhomogeneous, anisotropic Mat\'ern-like Gaussian random field. We provide a parametrized model for a torus-like disk and a central jet through a single composite correlation tensor. The resulting effective model is an implementation-ready prescription for time-dependent thick-disk and disk-jet emission for relativistic studies.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro C\'ardenas-Avenda\~no, Diego Rubiera-Garcia, Frederic H. Vincent

item.title: Resolving Galactic and Cluster Dynamics Without Dark Matter: Tsallis Entropy as the Unique Foundation of Emergent Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.19435v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While modified entropy models-such as Barrow, Tsallis, Kaniadakis,Power-law, Logarithmic, and R\'{e}nyi entropies-have been widely explored in cosmological contexts, their implications on galactic scales remain largely untested. These generalizations of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy encode quantum gravitational, nonextensive, or fractal spacetime effects and can alter the gravitational entropy-area relation. In this paper, we demonstrate that the entropic force framework, when applied to galactic rotation curves and the baryonic mass of galaxy clusters, uniquely selects Tsallis entropy as the specific generalized entropy formulation. We then extend this Tsallis modified gravity to globular clusters to complete the structural hierarchy from galaxies to galaxy clusters to globular clusters and to investigate its behavior as a function of system scale. We will show that the nonextensive parameter exhibits no correlation with any of the macroscopic quantities characterizing gravitational systems, such as mass, radius, temperature, or density. Furthermore, it has previously been shown that entropy is not well-defined within the standard thermodynamic approach to gravity. The adoption of nonextensive statistics provides a foundation for entanglement, thereby enabling a consistent definition of entanglement entropy. We predict the existence of galaxy clusters with $\delta = 1$ (i.e., clusters whose dynamics require no dark matter) analogous to $\delta = 1$ systems already observed at galactic and globular cluster scales. This prediction provides a unique observational test to discriminate Tsallis gravity from $\Lambda$CDM and MOND. Therefore, for the entropic gravity paradigm to be consistent with observational data across all scales-from globular clusters to galaxies to galaxy clusters-it is inevitably required to be built upon \textit{Tsallis} entropy.
item.dc:creator: S. Shamari, A. Sheykhi

item.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
item.description: arXiv:2607.25067v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ (leading) and $\Delta=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $\Delta=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $\Delta=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Manizheh Botshekananfard, Elif B\"u\c{s}ra G\"uraks{\i}n, Vasileios A. Letsios, Gizem \c{S}eng\"or

item.title: Primordial Black Hole Seeds for Little Red Dots in $f(R)$ Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.29727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The little red dots (LRDs) discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope host black holes of up to $10^{9}\,M_{\odot}$ within the first billion years, posing a challenge to conventional seeding scenarios. We investigate whether such seeds can form in dense clusters of primordial black holes (PBHs), in which the central object grows by gravitational capture of the surrounding PBHs while accreting gas, within Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ gravity, where the scalar field acts on the matter surrounding the PBHs. For the adopted cluster configuration, our results show that accretion and mergers reinforce one another: for time-averaged Eddington ratios $\lambda_{\rm Edd}\gtrsim0.3$, the seed consumes its cluster by $z\simeq5.5$-$7.3$ and subsequently grows into the LRD mass range. Calibrated on the observed black-hole mass function, the model reproduces the abundance of LRDs near the peak of their population without further adjustment, while it underpredicts the abundance at $z\simeq7.5$ and overpredicts it at $z\simeq2$. Our findings indicate that the earliest seeds may accrete about twice as efficiently as later ones, and that the finite cluster reservoir can imprint a lower edge on the mass function near the cluster mass. Within the adopted screening and halo-growth prescriptions, the scalar field enhances the abundance of active seeds by up to $\sim 13\%$ at lower redshifts and by $\sim 7\%$ at $z \simeq 7.5$ for the strongest model considered, modestly moving the high-redshift prediction towards the data at fixed normalization. Also, the remnant spins can further discriminate between feeding modes.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Fakhry

item.title: Forward Bayesian Inference for the Binary Black Hole Populations
item.description: arXiv:2610.03459v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present PopCWB, a Bayesian framework for the inference of the binary black hole (BBH) population based on the unmodeled search pipeline coherent WaveBurst (cWB). The standard population analysis takes an inverse approach by inferring the underlying population model parameters for a given set of detected events using the individual posterior samples. In PopCWB, we take a forward approach to population inference by varying population models to identify the most optimal one which describes the observed events. Rather than using event-level posterior samples, PopCWB uses a large set of simulated events reconstructed by cWB and their total mass, estimated with a machine-learning regression, to construct marginal probability distributions. These marginal probabilities are then used in the construction of the likelihood. We apply PopCWB to BBH events detected by cWB during the third observing run (O3) of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA detectors. We constrain an astrophysically motivated BBH population model that incorporates the effects of pulsational pair-instability supernovae and dynamical mergers. The analysis predicts a maximum black hole mass of $\mathbf{45.5^{+5.1}_{-6.1} M_{\odot}}$ from stellar evolution and an inferred local BBH merger rate of $\mathbf{23.0^{+16.6}_{-8.3} \, Gpc^{-3} yr^{-1}}$. We compare these results with the existing population models from the literature.
item.dc:creator: Poulami Dutta Roy, Tanmaya Mishra, Achal Kumar, Sergey Klimenko

item.title: Thermodynamics and mechanical laws of causal-diamond horizons
item.description: arXiv:2610.07746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a unified thermodynamic and mechanical framework for causal-diamond horizons in Minkowski spacetime. Euclidean regularity fixes the temperature $T_D=1/(\pi\alpha)$, where $2\alpha$ is the temporal extent of the diamond. The regulated Gibbons-Hawking-York contribution gives $I_D^E=-A_0/(4G)$, with $A_0$ the area of the horizon bifurcation surface, and the vanishing equilibrium geometric energy then yields the entropy-area relation $S_D=A_0/(4G)$. For weak matter perturbations crossing a localized portion of the future horizon, a Raychaudhuri analysis relates the associated Killing-energy flux to the area response, yielding a local physical-process first law at leading order near the bifurcation surface and, for classical matter satisfying the null energy condition, a local second law. Uniform conformal surface gravity establishes the zeroth law, while zero temperature is approached only in the limit $\alpha\to\infty$, in which the finite causal horizon disappears. These results show that a coherent horizon-law structure can arise within a causal diamond, a fundamental building block of the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime. The derivation is explicit in $(2+1)$ dimensions, while the physical results retain the same form for spherical causal diamonds in $d\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Carlos R. Ord\'o\~nez, Gustavo Valdivia-Mera

item.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.13867v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic and counterterm contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the VEGAS algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.20h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$, or $0.27h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.42h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for an emission line galaxy sample at $z=1.1$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $\sigma_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference.
item.dc:creator: Oliver H. E. Philcox

item.title: Finite-cutoff geometry in double-scaled SYK: SYK deformations, branes and CMC-Krylov complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.20703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a finite-cutoff holographic description of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We construct microscopic deformations of Kourkoulou-Maldacena and thermofield-double SYK states whose double-scaling limits reproduce a lower-dimensional analogue of $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}$ and $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}+\Lambda_2$ deformations, which we denote $T^2$ and $T^2+\Lambda_1$, respectively. The ensemble-averaged theory describes wormhole states in finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity, and finite-cutoff anti-de Sitter and de Sitter geometries in the low- and high-energy regimes, respectively. The analysis includes both perturbative and non-perturbative solutions to the energy spectrum flow equation, and the regions behind and beyond the respective horizons. Only the perturbative branch admits physical quantum states. We study how to incorporate end-of-the-world (ETW) branes in the finite cutoff holographic dictionary. The ETW brane leads to an additional boundary theory deformation, which leads to black hole or eternal traversable wormhole geometries depending on the existence of normalizable bound states. We extend the finite cutoff length evaluations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices, which we interpret as complexity in the boundary theory. We discuss possible extensions with matter. Our results provide a microscopic framework for studying the finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices and branes in the holographic dictionary of DSSYK.
item.dc:creator: Sergio E. Aguilar-Gutierrez

item.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.
item.dc:creator: Gert H\"utsi

item.title: Relativistic Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.28017v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Unruh effect links acceleration to thermalization, providing a relativistic setting for anomalous quantum relaxation. We demonstrate a {\it relativistic} strong quantum Mpemba effect in the Unruh thermalization of a two-level detector coupled to a massless scalar field. For a fixed pair of isospectral initial states, relaxation curves that never cross in inertial motion exhibit a Mpemba crossing above a threshold acceleration. At a higher, precisely tuned acceleration, the initially farther state has zero overlap with the slowest decay mode and relaxes with a faster asymptotic exponential rate. We identify how competition between transition and dephasing channels governs the relaxation spectrum, where sufficiently strong longitudinal coupling enables acceleration to switch the relaxation bottleneck between population and coherence modes. We derive the spectral-switching condition and construct isospectral preparation protocols that eliminate slow-mode contributions within their physical domains. Our results establish acceleration as a control parameter for anomalous quantum relaxation, connecting relativistic quantum dynamics with nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhilong Liu, Zehua Tian, Hui Jing, Jieci Wang
